Website scan report

Visible Google Chrome 135.0.7049.95 · 2026-11-04T05:54:57.468390+00:00

Downloaded bytes are Chrome-reported encoded HTTP response transfers for the monitored page target, including redirect hops and partial bytes where exposed. Cached/service-worker responses are identified and excluded from downloaded totals. Independent worker targets and out-of-process iframe targets are not instrumented in this version; their traffic/diagnostics may be incomplete. This is not a packet capture: TLS/TCP overhead, browser background traffic, and complete upload sizes are not included. WebSocket payloads and available upload payload estimates are separate. HTML sizes use decimal KB (1 KB = 1,000 bytes). Cache policy is recorded in run settings. Cold mode clears/disables the HTTP response cache and bypasses service workers for the measured tab. Dedicated profiles retain cookies/site storage; fresh contexts reset session state. OS/DNS, connections, and server/CDN caches are not reset. Current settling policy is the main document load event (plus any configured ready selector), followed by the configured observation delay, normally 15 seconds. Background requests do not extend it. This is a defined observation window, not a claim that animations or all network activity have stopped. Human-check waits pause the active timeout clocks; wall observation/settle times and totals include them. A load time after a challenge describes the final document, not the entire verification journey. Screenshots and report generation happen after the measurement window. Chrome's real Console opens only after observation; its screenshot can include messages emitted after the measured cutoff. Errors/warnings are occurrence counts; network failures and HTTP errors are separate counts and can describe the same underlying problem. Browser diagnostics are those exposed by CDP, not every DevTools panel.
